topic: Bajada Geomorphology & Piedmont Alluvial Fan Coalescence
question: ‘Bajada’ is a type of :
correct_text: Alluvial fan (Compound coalescing alluvial fan apron along a mountain piedmont)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 25); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 8, pp. 235-242)

topic: Braided Stream Morphology & Leopold-Wolman Threshold
question: A stream consisting of interwoven channels is known as :
correct_text: Braided stream (Multi-thread interwoven channels separated by mobile braid bars)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 25); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 8, pp. 244-248); Leopold & Wolman (1957)

topic: Canyon & Gorge Geomorphology: Vertical Bedrock Downcutting
question: A canyon is a :

options.A: A deep valley with vertical sides

correct_text: A deep valley with vertical sides (Steep-walled chasm carved by vertical river incision exceeding slope wasting)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 24); Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, pp. 524-528)

topic: Trellis Drainage Pattern & Structural Strike-Dip Control
question: A network of parallel or subparallel streams developed along strike and dip directions are known as :
correct_text: Trellis (Parallel master streams along strike joined at right angles by dip tributaries)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 27); Arthur L. Bloom (Geomorphology, Ch. 11, pp. 272-276)

topic: The Physics of Eustasy: Global Sea-Level Dynamics
question: The term ‘eustatic’ implies :
correct_text: Worldwide changes in sea level (Global synchronous sea-level changes driven by glacio-eustasy & tectono-eustasy)
textbook_ref: Eduard Suess (Das Antlitz der Erde, 1888); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 33); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 12)

topic: Glacial Fiords: Overdeepened Troughs & Marine Drowning
question: Fiords are formed due to :
correct_text: Glacial activity (Submerged U-shaped glacial troughs overdeepened below sea level with a shallow seaward sill)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 31); Arthur L. Bloom (Geomorphology, Ch. 15, pp. 378-384)

topic: Aeolian Granulometry: Bagnold Saltation Physics & Sand Sorting
question: Well sorted aeolian deposits are chiefly composed of :
correct_text: Sand (Medium to fine quartz sand concentrated into dunes via saltation while silt/clay is winnowed into suspension)
textbook_ref: Ralph A. Bagnold (The Physics of Blown Sand, 1941); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 23); Sam Boggs Jr. (Ch. 8, pp. 268-274)

topic: Horton's Drainage Density & Basin Morphometry
question: Drainage density of a basin is a measure of :

options.A: Total number of the highest order streams divided by the total number of the next lower order streams
options.B: Length of the largest stream divided by the total area of the basin
options.C: Total length of streams of all orders divided by the total area of the basin
options.D: Total number of streams of all orders

correct_text: Total length of streams of all orders divided by the total area of the basin (Horton, 1945: D_d = ΣL / A)
textbook_ref: Robert E. Horton (GSA Bulletin, 1945); Arthur N. Strahler (GSA Bulletin, 1957); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 27)

topic: Glacial Moraines, Till Dynamics & Depositional Landforms
question: Moraines are formed in :
correct_text: Glacial Environment (Unsorted, unstratified till/diamicton ridges deposited by glacial ice)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 32); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 8, pp. 275-282)

topic: Karst Topography, Carbonate Thermodynamics & Speleothems
question: Karst topography is most commonly developed in :
correct_text: Limestone bearing areas (Subterranean dissolution of soluble CaCO3 by carbonic acid forming sinkholes & caves)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 38); Derek Ford & Paul Williams (Karst Hydrogeology and Geomorphology, 2007)

topic: Aeolian Dune Classification: Barchans & Transverse Wind Dynamics
question: A sand dune with its long axis transverse to wind direction is called :
correct_text: Barchan (Crescentic dune with crest axis oriented transverse to wind and horns pointing downwind)
textbook_ref: Ralph A. Bagnold (The Physics of Blown Sand, 1941); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 23); Sam Boggs Jr. (Ch. 8, pp. 268-274)

topic: Glaciofluvial Eskers: Subglacial Pressurized Channel Drift
question: Esker is a :

options.D: Alluvial deposit rich in clay matter

correct_text: Glaciofluvial deposit (Stratified sand and gravel ridge deposited by subglacial meltwater streams)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 32); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 8, pp. 280-285)

topic: Speleothem Morphogenesis: Stalactites, Stalagmites & Karst Solution
question: Development of stalactite and stalagmite is associated with :
correct_text: Solution activity (Chemical dissolution of carbonate rock followed by CO2 degassing and calcite precipitation)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 38); Derek Ford & Paul Williams (Karst Hydrogeology and Geomorphology, 2007)

topic: Mechanics of Mass Wasting: Gravitational Driving Forces & Limit Equilibrium
question: Mass wasting is primarily affected by :
correct_text: Force of gravity (Direct downslope movement of rock and soil driven by gravitational shear stress)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 377-380); Karl Terzaghi (Theoretical Soil Mechanics, 1943); D.J. Varnes (1978)

topic: Dendritic Drainage Networks: Structural Isotropy & Topologic Branching
question: If a region is lacking in structural control, then the drainage pattern in such regions will be :
correct_text: Dendritic (Tree-like branching network developing on homogeneous, structurally isotropic rocks)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 27); Arthur L. Bloom (Geomorphology, Ch. 11, pp. 272-276)

topic: Volcanic Calderas: Summit Collapse & Magma Chamber Drainage
question: A Caldera is :

options.C: A gorge formed due to faulting

correct_text: A very large crater (Large basin-shaped collapse depression formed by roof subsidence into an evacuated magma chamber)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 15); Gordon A. Macdonald (Volcanoes, 1972); Peter W. Lipman (1997)

topic: Fault Rocks: Rock Flour, Fault Gouge & Brittle Cataclasis
question: Rock flour or gouge is closely linked to :
correct_text: Brittle deformation (Mechanical pulverization, crushing, and frictional grinding in upper crustal shear zones)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 215); Marland P. Billings (Structural Geology, pp. 150-154); Richard H. Sibson (1977)

topic: Fault Plane Attitude: Hade, Dip & Coordinate Transformations
question: The angle which the fault plane makes with vertical plane is known as :
correct_text: Hade (Complement of the dip angle: Hade = 90° - Dip)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 208); Marland P. Billings (Structural Geology, pp. 138-142)

topic: Normal Faulting Kinematics & Andersonian Extensional Tectonics
question: If the hanging wall in a fault is in downthrown side, it is called :
correct_text: Normal fault (Dip-slip fault where hanging wall moves downward relative to footwall under extensional stress)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 209); E.M. Anderson (The Dynamics of Faulting, 1905); Haakon Fossen (Ch. 9)

topic: Fold Geometry: Hinge Lines, Fold Axes & Profile Planes
question: The line which is parallel to the hinge in a fold is called :
correct_text: Axis of the fold (The imaginary line generator which is parallel to the hinge line in cylindrical folds)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 185); Marland P. Billings (Structural Geology, pp. 35-42); John G. Ramsay (1967)

topic: Recumbent Folds: Horizontal Axial Planes & Nappe Tectonics
question: If the axial plane of the fold is horizontal, then it is said to be :
correct_text: Recumbent fold (Fold with subhorizontal axial plane, dip <10°, and completely inverted lower limb)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 190); M.J. Fleuty (Proceedings of the Geologists' Association, 1964)

topic: Unconformity Taxonomy: Blended Contacts & Paleosol Preservation
question: A contact of younger sediments deposited over a thick residual soil that grades into underlying bedrock is called :
correct_text: Blended unconformity (Transitional, fuzzy contact preserving in-situ residual soil grading downward into bedrock)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 225); Dunbar & Rodgers (Principles of Stratigraphy, 1957); Sam Boggs Jr. (Ch. 12)

topic: Tectonic Fabric: Bedding-Cleavage Intersection Lineations (L0xS1)
question: The intersection of bedding and cleavage produces :
correct_text: Lineation (Intersection lineation parallel to fold hinge line formed by intersection of S0 bedding and S1 cleavage)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 235); John G. Ramsay & Martin I. Huber (Vol. 2, 1983); Marland P. Billings (pp. 340-345)

topic: Fault Classification: High-Angle vs. Low-Angle (45° Threshold)
question: High angle faults are those that dip greater than :
correct_text: 45 degree (High-angle faults dip >45° where throw exceeds heave; low-angle faults dip ≤45° where heave exceeds throw)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 212); Marland P. Billings (Structural Geology, pp. 145-148); Haakon Fossen (Ch. 9)

topic: Conjugate Folds: Box Folds & Multiple Hinge Lines
question: In which fold there could be two hinges ?
correct_text: Box fold (Conjugate fold possessing two distinct hinge lines and two intersecting axial surfaces bounding a flat crest or trough)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (p. 115); Marland P. Billings (p. 61); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Earth Structure, p. 259)

topic: Fold Rheology: Disharmonic & Similar Folds (Hinge Thickening)
question: Thickened crests and troughs with thinner limbs are noticed in:
correct_text: Disharmonic fold (Incompetent strata undergo plastic ductile flow from limbs into crests and troughs, producing pronounced hinge thickening)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 114); Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, p. 248); John G. Ramsay (Class 2 Folds)

topic: Denudation Structures: Inlier vs. Outlier Map Patterns
question: On a geological map, if older strata are found to be surrounded by younger strata then it could be :
correct_text: An inlier (An exposure of older rocks completely surrounded by younger strata on a map, formed by erosion unroofing anticlines, domes, or valleys)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 124, Fig 7.49); Marland P. Billings (p. 89); P.K. Mukherjee (p. 182)

topic: Plate Tectonics: Horst, Graben & Divergent Boundary Rifting
question: Horst and Graben structures are mainly confined to:
correct_text: Divergent boundaries (Extensional regimes with vertical maximum stress trigger conjugate normal faults, producing horsts and graben rift valleys)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 119); Haakon Fossen (p. 172); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (p. 430)

topic: Plutonic Fracturing: Sheet Joints & Exfoliation in Granite
question: Granite usually exhibits :
correct_text: Sheet joints (Curvilinear fractures parallel to ground topography formed by elastic rebound and lithostatic pressure release during unroofing)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 123); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Earth Structure, p. 163, Fig 7.7); Marland P. Billings

topic: Fold Attitude: Plunging Folds & Inclined Hinge Lines
question: The fold is said to have plunge if :
correct_text: The axis is not horizontal (A fold has a plunge if its hinge line/axis is inclined to the horizontal plane, causing V-shaped map outcrop closures)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 113, Fig 7.8); Marland P. Billings (p. 53); Haakon Fossen (p. 238)

topic: Paleogeography: Pangea Rifting into Laurasia & Gondwanaland
question: The two super continental blocks separated due to drifting are :
correct_text: Laurasia and Gondwanaland (Early Mesozoic Tethyan rifting split Pangea into northern Laurasia and southern Gondwanaland)
textbook_ref: Alfred Wegener (1915); Eduard Suess (1885); K.M. Bangar (p. 28); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Earth Structure, p. 580)

topic: Earth's Thermal Engine: Convective Venting along Mid-Ocean Ridges
question: The convection energy of the earth is commonly released along:
correct_text: Divergent boundaries in oceans (Mid-ocean ridge spreading axes release over 70% of Earth's internal convective heat via decompression magma & hydrothermal venting)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (p. 30); C.M.R. Fowler (The Solid Earth, Ch. 7); Turcotte & Schubert (Geodynamics); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (p. 438)

topic: Planetary Discontinuities: The Mohorovicic Boundary (Moho)
question: Mohorovicic discontinuity separates :
correct_text: Crust and Mantle (Major seismic discontinuity where P-wave velocity jumps abruptly from ~6.8 km/s in the lower crust to ~8.1 km/s in uppermost peridotite mantle)
textbook_ref: Andrija Mohorovičić (1909); K.M. Bangar (p. 23); John D. Winter (Petrology, p. 3); C.M.R. Fowler (p. 102)

topic: Rheological Stratification: Asthenosphere in the Upper Mantle
question: The asthenospheric layer inclued :
correct_text: Upper mantle beneath lithosphere (Ductile, mechanically weak layer of the upper mantle between ~100 km and 410 km depth enabling plate drift)
textbook_ref: Joseph Barrell (1914); K.M. Bangar (p. 25); C.M.R. Fowler (The Solid Earth, p. 104); Turcotte & Schubert (Geodynamics)

topic: Planetary Density Distribution: Earth's Core Density (10.7 g/cm³)
question: An average density of 1 0.7 gmicm? prevails at:
correct_text: Core (Under the PREM model, density ranges from 9.9 to 12.2 g/cm³ in the outer core, averaging precisely 10.7 g/cm³)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 24); Dziewonski & Anderson (PREM, 1981); C.M.R. Fowler (p. 110)

topic: Physical Weathering: Exfoliation & Spheroidal Spalling in Massive Rocks
question: The process of weathering by exfoliating activity is very effective in:
correct_text: Massive rocks (Homogeneous isotropic rocks devoid of bedding or foliation spall off curved concentric shells due to thermal insolation and chemical hydration stresses)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 20); G.B. Mahapatra (Textbook of Geology, p. 45); P.K. Mukherjee (p. 28)

topic: Eruption Mechanics: Pelean Type Volcanoes & Most Violent Activity
question: Pelean type of volcano is known for:
correct_text: Most violent activity (Characterized by extremely viscous dacitic lava spines, catastrophic dome collapses, lateral blasts, and incandescent nuées ardentes)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 49); Cas & Wright (Volcanic Successions); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 55)

topic: Volcanic Edifices: Stratovolcanoes & Composite Cone Architecture
question: Composite cones are the characteristics of :
correct_text: Strato volcanoes (Stratified conical edifices constructed from alternating layers of explosive pyroclastic tephra and solidified intermediate/felsic lava flows)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 48); Tarbuck & Lutgens (Earth Science); Philpotts & Ague (Igneous Petrology)

topic: Isostasy: Airy's Model of Mountain Roots & Flotation in Denser Substratum
question: According to Airy’s theory of isostasy :

options.A: Lighter mountains are floating on the lighter substratum
options.B: Lighter mountains are floating on the denser substratum
options.C: Denser mountains are floating on denser substratum
options.D: Denser mountains are floating on the lighter substratum

correct_text: Lighter mountains are floating on the denser substratum (Light crustal rocks of uniform density ~2.8 g/cm³ float in hydrostatic equilibrium upon a denser ~3.3 g/cm³ mantle substratum, supported by deep roots)
textbook_ref: Sir George Biddell Airy (1855); K.M. Bangar (p. 32); C.M.R. Fowler (The Solid Earth, p. 195); Turcotte & Schubert (Geodynamics)

topic: Continental Margins: Atlantic Passive Margin Architecture
question: The Atlantic continental margin of North America is known to be :
correct_text: Passive margin (Stable intraplate trailing margin devoid of active subduction, volcanism, or trenches, featuring wide continental shelves and thick post-rift sedimentary prisms)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 34); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Earth Structure, p. 437); Sam Boggs Jr. (p. 434)

topic: Planetary Hypsometry: Average Depth of the Global Ocean (3,729 m)
question: The average depth of the ocean is:
correct_text: 3,729 meters (Classical geodetic datum representing total oceanic volume divided by oceanic surface area, forming the lower peak of Earth's bimodal hypsographic curve)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 35); Sverdrup, Johnson & Fleming (The Oceans, 1942); Thurman & Trujillo (Oceanography)

topic: Paleomagnetism: Geomagnetic Pole Reversals & Seafloor Striping
question: Palaeomagnetic data is useful for understanding :
correct_text: Pole reversals (Thermo-remanent magnetization in basalt records spontaneous flips of Earth's magnetic dipole, proving the Vine-Matthews-Morley seafloor spreading hypothesis)
textbook_ref: Bernard Brunhes (1906); Motonori Matuyama (1929); K.M. Bangar (p. 28); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Earth Structure, p. 445)

topic: Seamount Morphometry: Guyots as Wave-Beveled Flat-Topped Seamounts
question: Guyot is a :

options.B: Major depression in a continental area
options.D: Flat topped hill on the surface

correct_text: Flat topped seamount (Submerged volcanic mountain whose peak was beveled flat by wave action at sea level and subsequently drowned to deep water by lithospheric thermal subsidence)
textbook_ref: Harry H. Hess (1946); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 36); Thurman & Trujillo (Essentials of Oceanography)

topic: Subduction Geomorphology: Deep Sea Trenches of the Circum-Pacific Belt
question: Deep sea trenches are generally associated with :
correct_text: Circum pacific belt (Over 80% of Earth's oceanic deep-sea trenches encircle the Pacific Ocean basin along convergent subduction zones consuming oceanic lithosphere)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 36 & p. 50); C.M.R. Fowler (The Solid Earth); Tarbuck & Lutgens (Earth Science)

topic: Crustal Geothermics: Temperature in the Upper Lower Crust (400-500°C)
question: The temperature regime in the upper part of the lower crust is:
correct_text: 400-500°C (Under standard continental geothermal gradients of 20-25°C/km, depths of 20-25 km at the Conrad discontinuity reach 400° to 500°C, marking plagioclase plastic creep)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 22); John D. Winter (Petrology, Ch. 1, p. 5); C.M.R. Fowler (The Solid Earth, p. 235)

topic: Dharwar Craton Stratigraphy & Youngest Event: Closepet Granite (~2.51 Ga)
question: Which of the following represents the youngest event in the Dharwarian stratigraphy ?
correct_text: Closepet Granite (Late-to-post-tectonic granite batholith dated at 2.51 Ga, terminating Dharwar cratonization)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 277-279); M. Ramakrishnan & R. Vaidyanadhan (Geology of India, Vol. 1, pp. 79-115)

topic: Chronostratigraphic Pair: Niniyur Formation & Cretaceous-Tertiary Marine Transition
question: Choose the correct pair of stratigraphic formation and its corresponding age :
correct_text: Niniyur Formation — Cretaceous (Uppermost terminal division of the classic Cauvery Basin Cretaceous-Tertiary marine succession in Trichinopoly)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 296); M.S. Krishnan (Geology of India and Burma, pp. 410-425)

topic: Kutch Basin: Global Type Area for the Indian Jurassic System
question: Kutch is the type Area in India for :
correct_text: Jurassic formation (Iconic Patcham, Chari, Katrol, and Umia Formations with world-standard cephalopod ammonite biozones)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 291-293); W. Waagen (Jurassic Fauna of Kutch, Pal. Ind.)

topic: Siwalik Foreland Molasse: Global Treasury of Mammal Fossils
question: Siwaliks are well known for:
correct_text: Mammal fossils (World's richest Neogene terrestrial record: Sivapithecus hominoids, Hipparion and Equus horses, Stegodon elephants, bovids)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 302-304); G.E. Pilgrim & E.H. Colbert (Siwalik Vertebrates)

topic: Spiti Tethyan Basin: Permian System Represented by Kuling Group
question: In Spiti, the Permians are represented by :
correct_text: Kuling group (Comprises the basal Gechang sandstone and upper Gungri / Productus Shales with Cyclolobus and Marginifera)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 287-288); S.V. Srikantia & O.N. Bhargava (Geology of Spiti)

topic: Aravalli-Delhi Orogenic Belt: Delhi System Intrusion by Erinpura Granite
question: Dalhi system is intruded by:
correct_text: Erinpura Granite (Post-tectonic Neoproterozoic calc-alkaline batholiths dated at ~850-800 Ma cross-cutting folded Delhi metasediments)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 280-281); A.M. Heron (Geology of Central Rajputana, GSI Memoir 79)

topic: Lithofacies Analysis: Mesozoic Bhuj Formation Predominantly Sandstones
question: Which of the following statement is correct ?

options.A: The Mesozoic Bhuj formation consists predominantly of sandstones
options.B: Kaladgi basin is predominantly made of slates
options.C: Vindhyan supergroup is devoid of limestone
options.D: Cuddapah basin is predominantly made of metadacites

correct_text: The Mesozoic Bhuj formation consists predominantly of sandstones (Thick, cross-bedded fluvial to deltaic quartzose sandstones with minor plant shales)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 297); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 5)

topic: Muth Quartzite: Devonian Regional Marker Horizon in the Himalaya
question: Marker horizon for Devonian in Himalaya is called ;
correct_text: Muth quartzites (Ubiquitous snow-white super-mature quartz arenite cliff-former across Kashmir, Spiti, Zanskar, and Kumaon)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 286); F. Stoliczka (Mem. GSI, 1865)

topic: Stromatolites: Direct Windows into the Origin and Evolution of Life
question: Stromatolites provide insight for:

options.B: Recognizing boundary between Cambrian and Ordovician

correct_text: Origin and Evolution of life (Organo-sedimentary laminations constructed by cyanobacteria dating back to 3.5 Ga in Archean cherts)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 273-274); Sam Boggs Jr. (Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 6, p. 195)

topic: Main Boundary Thrust (MBT) Juxtaposing Siwaliks and Lesser Himalaya
question: In Himalayas, the main boundary fault separates ;
correct_text: Siwalik and Tertiary (Crustal-scale thrust fault placing the Lesser Himalayan pre-Tertiary and Paleogene belt over the Sub-Himalayan Siwalik molasse)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 306-307); B.A. van der Pluijm & S. Marshak (Earth Structure, Ch. 21)

topic: Deccan Large Igneous Province: Cretaceous Volcanic Eruptive Pulse
question: The Volumincus Deccan Flood Basalts occurred during :
correct_text: Cretaceous (Massive tholeiitic outpourings spanning 66.4 to 64.5 Ma across the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian and K-Pg boundary)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 297-299); John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 15)

topic: Mesozoic-Cenozoic (K-Pg) Boundary at Approximately 65 Ma
question: Mesozoic and Cenozoic boundary lies approximately at :
correct_text: 65 Ma (Precisely calibrated at 66.0 Ma in ICS chronostratigraphy, marked by the Chicxulub bolide impact and iridium anomaly)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 272); International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS Time Scale 2024)

topic: Salkhala Series: Archean-Precambrian Crystalline Basement of Kashmir-Hazara
question: In Kashmir-Hazara area, the Archean rocks are called:
correct_text: Salkhala series (Metamorphic complex of graphitic schists, phyllites, crystalline marbles, and gneisses underlying the Dogra Slates)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 281); D.N. Wadia (Geology of India, pp. 112-120)

topic: Precambrian Supereon Occupying the Longest Time Period (>88% of History)
question: in the geological history, which of the following occupies longest time period.?
correct_text: Precambrian (Spans ~4,000 million years from 4.54 Ga to 539 Ma, representing over 88% of all geological time on Earth)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 273); Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology)

topic: Cretaceous-Tertiary (K-Pg) Boundary Mass Extinction Event
question: Which of the following is known to be the boundary of mass extinction ?
correct_text: Cretaceous — Tertiary (Wiped out 76% of species including non-avian dinosaurs, ammonites, and marine reptiles at ~66 Ma)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 299); L. Alvarez et al. (Science, 1980)

topic: Archaeocyatha Confined to Lower Palaeozoic (Cambrian)
question: Archaeocyatha is confined to :
correct_text: Lower Palaeozoic (Earth's earliest skeletal reef-building poriferans strictly restricted to the Cambrian Period ~525-505 Ma)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 260-261); Clarkson (Invertebrate Palaeontology)

topic: Class Trilobita Geological Range (Cambrian to Permian)
question: Trilobites lived during :
correct_text: Cambrian to Permian (Appeared in Early Cambrian ~521 Ma and went completely extinct at the End-Permian P-Tr boundary ~252 Ma)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 267-270); Fortey (Trilobite: Eyewitness to Evolution)

topic: First Tetrapods to Colonize Land: Amphibia (Labyrinthodontia)
question: The first group of tetrapods to colonize the land successfully are :
correct_text: Amphibia (Stem amphibians such as Ichthyostega and Acanthostega developed dactylic limbs and lungs in Late Devonian ~365 Ma)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 271-272); Benton (Vertebrate Palaeontology, Ch. 4)

topic: Class Crinoidea Geological Range (Cambrian to Recent)
question: Crinoids range in age from :
correct_text: Cambrian to recent (Sea lilies and feather stars originated in the Early Cambrian and flourish in modern oceans with >600 living species)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 265-266); Clarkson (Invertebrate Palaeontology)

topic: Epizoic Organisms: Living Attached to Another Living Host
question: Organisms which live attached to another larger organism are known as :
correct_text: Epizoic (Non-parasitic attachment to external body surfaces of living host organisms, such as barnacles on whales or bryozoans on shells)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 259); Dodd & Stanton (Paleoecology: Concepts and Applications)

topic: Plankton Mode of Life & Water-Column Ecological Divisions
question: Plankton generally refers to :
correct_text: Free swimming organisms [Pelagic water-column organisms; passive drifters unable to swim against horizontal currents, predominantly unicellular]
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 258); Thurman & Trujillo (Essentials of Oceanography)

topic: Equine Evolution: Hyracotherium (Eohippus) as the First Stage
question: In the evolution of horse which of the following was the first stage ?
correct_text: Hyracotherius (Hyracotherium / Eohippus: Early Eocene dawn horse with 4 front toes, 3 hind toes, and low-crowned brachydont teeth)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 272-273); Simpson (Horses: The Story of the Horse Family)

topic: Buriadia: Primitive Conifer of the Lower Gondwana Flora
question: Amongst the following flora which represents a conifer ?
correct_text: Buriadia (Buriadia sewardii: Early Permian conifer with bifid needle-like leaves and solitary terminal seeds from Karharbari beds)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 290-291); Birbal Sahni (Palaeobotanica Indica)

topic: Ramapithecus (Sivapithecus) as a Fossil Primate
question: Which of the following is primate fossil?
correct_text: Ramapithecus (Hominoid ape discovered in the Middle Siwaliks of Haritalyangar, Himachal Pradesh, sharing ancestry with orangutans)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 303); Pilgrim & Lewis (Siwalik Primates)

topic: Ammonoid Sutures: Complex Frilled Evolution in the Mesozoic Period
question: Sutures of the ammonoids belonging to which period are an important feature in recognizing their evolution ?
correct_text: Mesozoic (Mesozoic ammonitic sutures feature multi-order frilled lobes and saddles serving as master index biozones in Jurassic & Cretaceous)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 263-264); Arkell (Mesozoic Ammonoidea)

topic: Physa Gastropod Exhibits Sinistral (Left-Handed) Coiling
question: Physa-the gastropod genus shows :
correct_text: Sinistrally coiled (Left-handed aperture opening when apex is upright; diagnostic index fossil Physa prinsepii in Deccan Intertrappeans)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 262); Cox (Treatise on Invertebrate Paleontology: Gastropoda)

topic: Class Articulata Characterized by Articulating Dental System
question: Which of the following Brachiopod has dental system ?
correct_text: Articulata (Valves articulate along hinge line with calcareous teeth on pedicle valve fitting into dental sockets on brachial valve)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 264-265); Williams & Rowell (Brachiopod Anatomy)

topic: Conodont is a Phosphatic Microfossil Composed of Carbonate-Apatite
question: Conodontis a: (Conodont is a :)
correct_text: Phosphatic microfossil (Microscopic teeth of primitive agnathan chordates composed of carbonate-apatite / francolite)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 270); Sweet (The Conodonta: Morphology, Taxonomy, Paleoecology)

topic: Arca: Classic Representative of Comb-Like Taxodont Dentition
question: Which amongst the following is a bivalve genus having taxodont type dentition ?
correct_text: Arca (Ark clams characterized by a continuous straight hinge plate with numerous small, similar, alternating transverse teeth and sockets)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 261); Moore (Treatise on Invertebrate Paleontology: Bivalvia)

topic: Ichnofossil is a Trace Fossil Represented by Footprints and Trails
question: Echnofossilis a: (Ichnofossil is a :)
correct_text: Fossilized horse foot print [and Fossilized serpent trail: Trace fossils recording biological locomotion/behavior rather than skeletal body parts]
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 257-258); Seilacher (Trace Fossil Analysis)

topic: Acid Igneous Rocks: 10% or More Free Quartz Criterion
question: Generally, acid igneous rocks contain :
correct_text: 10% or more free quartz (Acid rocks have >65-66% total silica, saturating all silicate bases and yielding at least 10% modal free quartz)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, pp. 110-112); John D. Winter (Igneous Petrology)

topic: Andesite is an Intermediate Volcanic Rock
question: Andesite is :

options.A: A coarse grained acid plutonic rock

correct_text: An intermediate volcanic rock (52-63 wt% SiO2, fine-grained/porphyritic extrusive equivalent of diorite characteristic of subduction arcs)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology); K.M. Bangar (p. 125)

topic: Bowen's Continuous Reaction Series: Calcic Plagioclase First Formed
question: The first mineral formed in the continuous series of Bowen reaction principle is :
correct_text: Calcic plagioclase (Pure anorthite CaAl2Si2O8 has highest melting point ~1553°C and crystallizes first from cooling basic melt)
textbook_ref: N.L. Bowen (1928, The Evolution of the Igneous Rocks); John D. Winter (Igneous Petrology)

topic: Carbonatite: Magmatic Carbonate Rock & REE Mineralization
question: A magmatic rock rich in calcium carbonate and often containing rare earth minerals is :
correct_text: Carbonatite (Mantle-derived igneous rock containing >50% modal carbonate minerals, hosting world-class reserves of REEs and Niobium)
textbook_ref: Keith Bell (Carbonatites); K.M. Bangar (p. 128); Winter (Igneous Petrology)

topic: Charnockite Mineral Composition: Quartz-Feldspar-Hypersthene
question: Generally, a charnockite has a mineral composition of :
correct_text: Quartz-Feldspar-Hypersthene (Sir Thomas Holland's hypersthene-bearing granite formed under high-grade dry granulite facies conditions)
textbook_ref: Sir Thomas Holland (1900, Memoirs of GSI); K.M. Bangar; Winter (Metamorphic Petrology)

topic: Diorite 100% Ferromagnesian Content: Perkinite
question: If the ferromagnesian content of diorite is 100%, then it is called :
correct_text: Perkinite (An ultramafic amphibole-pyroxene plutonic rock representing the 100% ferromagnesian, feldspar-free end-member of diorite)
textbook_ref: P.K. Mukherjee (A Textbook of Geology, p. 249); L. Duparc (1907); K.M. Bangar

topic: Dolerite Compositional Equivalence to Basalt
question: By mineral composition, dolerite is equivalent to :
correct_text: Basalt (Dolerite is the medium-grained hypabyssal intrusive equivalent of extrusive volcanic basalt, both consisting of labradorite + augite)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 126); John D. Winter (Igneous Petrology)

topic: Beerbachite is a Variety of Gabbro
question: Beerbachite is a variety of :
correct_text: Gabbro (A fine-grained, granular/aplitic microgabbro or pyroxene-hornfels composed of equigranular labradorite and pyroxene)
textbook_ref: C. Chelius (1892); P.K. Mukherjee (A Textbook of Geology, p. 251); IUGS Systematics

topic: Adamellite (Quartz Monzonite): Equal Amounts of Oligoclase & K-feldspar
question: Adamellite contains :

options.A: Roughly equal amounts of Oligoclase and K-feldspar
options.B: Roughly equal amounts of Quartz and Oligoclase
options.C: Roughly equal amounts of Quartz and K-feldspar
options.D: Roughly equal amounts of Quartz and Albite

correct_text: Roughly equal amounts of Oligoclase and K-feldspar (QAPF Field 3b Quartz Monzonite with P/(A+P) ratio between 35% and 65%)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 123); IUGS Systematics (Le Maitre, 2002)

topic: Graphic Texture Normally Exhibited by Pegmatite
question: Graphic texture is normally exhibited by :
correct_text: Pegmatite (Runic cuneiform intergrowth formed by simultaneous eutectic crystallization of quartz rods within microcline host)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 115); John D. Winter (Igneous Petrology)

topic: Laccolith: Igneous Body that has Domed Up Overlying Strata
question: An igneous body that has doomed up the strata into which it has been inserted is known as :
correct_text: Laccolith (Concordant plano-convex blister-like intrusion with a flat floor and an arched/domed roof flexing overlying strata)
textbook_ref: G.K. Gilbert (1877, Henry Mountains); K.M. Bangar (p. 118); G.B. Mahapatra

topic: Magmatic Stoping: Process Whereby Magma Works Way into Crust
question: A process whereby magma works its way up into the crust of the earth is known as :
correct_text: Magmatic stoping (R.A. Daly's mechanism of thermal shattering, overhead block detachment, and gravitational sinking of country rock xenoliths)
textbook_ref: R.A. Daly (1903, 1914); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 119)

topic: Minette is a Type of Lamprophyre
question: Minette is a type of :
correct_text: Lamprophyre (Calc-alkaline lamprophyre characterized by essential biotite/phlogopite phenocrysts in an orthoclase-dominated groundmass)
textbook_ref: N.M.S. Rock (1991, Lamprophyres); K.M. Bangar (p. 128); John D. Winter

topic: Palingenesis: Complete or Partial Melting of Pre-Existing Rock
question: The process of complete or partial melting of a rock is known as :
correct_text: Palingenesis (J.J. Sederholm's classical term for the rebirth/remelting of pre-existing crustal rocks to generate new magmatic melts)
textbook_ref: J.J. Sederholm (1907); P.K. Mukherjee (A Textbook of Geology, p. 238); K.M. Bangar

topic: Liquid Immiscibility: Unmixing of Two Liquids of Different Composition
question: Liquid imissibility generally results from :

options.A: Mixing of two liquids of two different composition
options.B: Mixing of two liquids of same composition
options.C: Unmixing of two liquids of different composition
options.D: Unmixing of two liquids of same composition

correct_text: Unmixing of two liquids of different composition (Thermodynamic solvus phenomenon where a parent melt splits into two distinct, mutually insoluble liquid phases)
textbook_ref: Edwin Roedder (1979); John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology); K.M. Bangar
